clue.text: Lady went along with me stumbling

indicators.note: stumbling suggests a lurching, disordered gait, so the letters of the words around it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lady is walking unsteadily beside the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' rearranges WENT, ALONG and ME; 'with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentlewoman is a woman of good birth or refined manners, a polite synonym for a lady.

clue.text: Muse to appear after a very long time

indicators.note: after places the word to behind the period of time in the answer

parts.note: an era is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: Inspiration arrives only after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: But role was abandoned causing bother

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so these letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor walking out of a part causes difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was abandoned' rearranges BUT and ROLE; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and bother both mean difficulty, fuss or inconvenience.

clue.text: Boy sent out after a word of hesitation

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the hesitation in the answer

parts.note: er is the sound made when hesitating

indicators.note: out suggests being out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy is sent away after someone hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a boy's name, so it serves for a lad or a male given name.

clue.text: Being GIs Norma upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some American soldiers have distressed a woman named Norma.
explanation.walkthrough: GIs are American soldiers in the surface; 'upset' rearranges GIS and NORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism is any living thing, a creature or being.

clue.text: Against most of one island or another

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: Guam is an island in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: Someone opposes much of one island in favour of a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims GUAM to GUA. The definition is 'another' (that is, another island), with 'or' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, a second island after the one in the wordplay.

clue.text: Arrived too late perhaps so had to fly?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for failing to take an opportunity in time
literally, a traveller who did not catch the ship must take a plane

explanation.surface: Being late, someone had to take a plane instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means losing a chance by delay, and literally a sailing was not caught, so air travel followed.

clue.text: Man shortly preparing for war-that's frightening

parts.note: Al is a short form of a man's name such as Alan or Albert
arming means equipping with weapons before conflict

explanation.surface: A man quickly getting ready for war is a scary sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarming means causing fear or anxiety, much like scary.

clue.text: Companions not here to be toasted

parts.note: absent means not present
friends are companions

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to companions who cannot be present.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the opposite order to the answer; the definition alludes to the traditional toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A common toast at gatherings honours loved ones who cannot attend.

clue.text: Woman briefly dwelling in state

parts.note: Ida is a woman's name
a dwelling is a house, and house is abbreviated HO

explanation.surface: A woman lives for a short while in some American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Dive for a weapon to use in the dark?

definitions.meaning: a dive is a seedy bar or drinking den open late

definitions.text: a weapon to use in the dark?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a club (cudgel) for night-time use

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a cudgel to wield after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a disreputable late-night venue and, punningly, a cosh for night-time are covered by the phrase.

clue.text: It is plain, boss could use the small bowl on the table

definitions.text: the small bowl on the table

indicators.note: the letters could be put to use in a new order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain-spoken boss says the small table bowl would come in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could use' rearranges PLAIN and BOSS; 'It is' merely opens the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A slop basin is a small bowl set on the tea table for emptying dregs from cups.

clue.text: Goes right round the plant

indicators.note: round, as in turned round, tells us these letters are spun into another order

explanation.surface: Someone walks right around the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal (R inside GOES gives GORES), but here it mixes GOES and R together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, also called furze or whin.

clue.text: Very quietly during bumpy ride find the bird

indicators.note: during says one piece occurs within the span of the other, so it sits inside
a bumpy ride shakes things up, so the letters of the word are jumbled

parts.note: PP is pianissimo, the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: On a jolting journey a birdwatcher quietly spots a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumpy' turns RIDE into DIER; 'during' puts PP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dipper is a small stream-dwelling songbird that walks underwater to feed.

clue.text: Outmoded fellow gave up the ghost

parts.note: passe means out of fashion
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person died.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up the ghost is an idiom for dying, and the phrasal verb is a euphemism for the same.

clue.text: One avoiding reality paces waywardly along one road

indicators.note: moving waywardly means going off course, so the letters of the word stray into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: A daydreamer wanders erratically along a single road.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapist seeks distraction from real life in fantasy or entertainment.

clue.text: Advance in French vehicle going round centre of Bourges

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: going round says the vehicle encloses the letter taken from the city

parts.note: a coach is a vehicle

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the town name

explanation.surface: A French car circles the middle of Bourges and moves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Bourges is a French city; its middle letter is R, which 'going round' puts inside COACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to advance gradually beyond proper limits, intruding on territory.

clue.text: Showing indecision about arranging the satin

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a fresh order, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone dithers about how to lay out a piece of satin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges the eight letters of THE SATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant describes someone wavering or uncertain before acting.

clue.text: Girl is a very long time with a piece of mosaic

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name
an era is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: A girl spends ages working on a mosaic piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or cubes that make up a mosaic.

clue.text: Redhead is hot stuff!

definitions.meaning: a red-haired person is nicknamed after the colour
a pungent spice that adds heat to food

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a red-haired person is very attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-haired person is nicknamed after a reddish colour, and the same word names a fiery root spice.

clue.text: I will break a leg although it is against the law

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will

indicators.note: break means smash apart, so these letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone vows to break a leg even though doing so is unlawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will' contracts to I'LL; 'break' turns A LEG into EGAL; 'although it is' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means forbidden by statute, unlawful.

clue.text: Webster?

parts.note: read as one who makes webs, rather than the surname of a dictionary maker

explanation.walkthrough: Webster is a surname (famous from the dictionary); read literally it is something that spins a web.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-legged creature spins silk nets to catch prey, so it is literally a web-maker.

clue.text: Consecrate Elizabeth being about 50

indicators.note: about says one name is placed around something else, enclosing it

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Elizabeth, near her half-century, is consecrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside BESS; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless something is to make it holy by a religious rite.

clue.text: Foolishly pulverise it being loathsome

indicators.note: acting foolishly means without order or sense, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Grinding it to dust stupidly is a disgusting thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive means causing disgust, the same as hateful or vile.

clue.text: The man is Bill accepting the key

indicators.note: accepting says the bill takes in the key, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: The man is presented with a bill along with the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's name, so it stands for a particular man.

clue.text: Coming before a stroke

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Coming before a stroke', gives AFORE from 'Coming before' (or A + FORE as a homophone of 'a four') but no word for SAID; a word such as 'said' appears to be missing from the OCR.

clue.text: Old-timer

parts.note: read literally, a timepiece that is old, rather than a veteran person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-timer' usually means a veteran; here it is a time-keeper of the old, tall, long-case kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-case pendulum clock is a traditional timekeeper, punningly an aged 'timer'.

clue.text: See 27
